title: What the program can do now

guide.text: Props are simple 3D shapes in the scene. They stand in for prims.
Box: good for a HUD, a board or a box.
guide.name: Box

guide.text: Sphere: good for a ball, a gag or a button.
guide.name: Sphere

guide.text: Cone: good for a hood, a hat or a bottle.
guide.name: Cone

guide.text: Torus, a ring: good for a cuff, a collar or a blindfold.
guide.name: Torus

guide.text: To add a prop, pick Props in the Joints panel. Press a shape button.
The program names it, for example Box 0 or Torus 0.
The next box is Box 1. You cannot change the name yet.
Place it with Position, Size and Turn in the Selected joint panel.
Pick a joint in Attach to. The prop then moves with that joint.
File, Save keeps the props in the animation file, names too. Open brings them back.
An object is a folder. Each folder inside it is one prim.
A prop and a prim with the same name belong together.
So a folder Box 0 goes with the prop Box 0.
The folder Root, or the object folder itself, is the main prim.
Show effects in 3D view is on the Live scripts page.
Tick it while a folder is watched. Props then show the scripts' colours.
They also show how clear a script made the prim.
Untick it and the props get their own colour back.
First colour works now: add one box, then watch that folder.
The other examples need props with names like Wrist_left.
Show effects in 3D view makes those props from the prim folders.
A made prop is a simple shape. Its place is a guess.
Clicking a prop is a touch only while Show effects is on.
A prop jumps to its new place. It does not glide there.
Touch, Say and dialog buttons do not reach a watched folder yet.
They reach only scripts that an AI assistant started.
